title: Gnosis Pay Reveals Customer Data Breach Weeks Before Card Service Shutdown
text:
Gnosis Pay Reveals Customer Data Breach Weeks Before Card Service Shutdown — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Market Influencers Gnosis Pay Reveals Customer Data Breach Weeks Before Card Service Shutdown
 Add preferred source Gnosis Pay said unauthorized access to its legacy consumer card system was detected on Nov. 3 and disclosed on Nov. 6, exposing customer information while leaving funds and the enterprise white-label platform untouched. Affected customers were emailed individually, and the company says it has contacted partners, its card issuer and data protection authorities. Online card payments now require 3D Secure until the consumer system is retired on Dec. 20, a closure announced in September. The incident is separate from a June exploit of about $1.5 million tied to the Zodiac smart contract framework, for which customers were reimbursed. Key Elements 
 Gnosis Pay 3D Secure Zodiac Safe help@gnosispay.com Gnosis Pay has disclosed that unauthorized parties accessed customer information on its legacy consumer card system, an incident that surfaced roughly six weeks before the company is scheduled to retire the platform on Dec. 20.
 The company said monitoring systems flagged the intrusion on Nov. 3 and that containment began within two hours. Affected credentials were replaced and the underlying vulnerability was addressed, according to the disclosure published Nov. 6. Customer funds were not affected, Gnosis Pay said, and its enterprise platform, which runs white-label card programs for other businesses, was not involved.
 Every affected customer received an individual email on Nov. 6 describing what information had been taken from their account. The public statement did not specify how many customers were impacted or list the categories of data exposed. Gnosis Pay said it had notified its partners and was in contact with the relevant data protection authorities and its card issuer.
 "We deeply regret that this happened," the company said in its announcement, adding that safeguarding personal information carries the same weight as protecting funds.
 Added verification on online purchases
 Online card payments now require 3D Secure, an extra identity-verification step at checkout, and the company said the requirement will stay in force until the consumer system shuts down. Card activity and wallets are also under closer scrutiny for fraud or attempts to reach customer balances, and Gnosis Pay said it has arranged specialist monitoring for signs that the leaked data is being misused.
 Customers were told to treat unexpected emails, texts, calls or letters about Gnosis Pay, partner apps or their cards with suspicion, and to navigate directly to the official web app or partner app instead of clicking links. The company said neither it nor its partners would ask for seed phrases, private keys, PINs or full card numbers, nor would they request re-verification of identity by email or text or instruct anyone to move funds over the phone or through messages.
 Shutdown timetable predates the breach
 The end date for the branded card program was set well before the November incident. A formal notice issued Sept. 21 scheduled the termination of branded card services for 23:59 UTC on Dec. 20, 2026. Physical and virtual cards will stop authorizing transactions at that point. Withdrawal functions will remain available in the web app, and customers keep ownership of assets held in their self-custodial Safe accounts.
 Cardholders who want continued card access must move to a partner program under new terms. The migration is optional, but existing branded cards will cease working regardless.
 Milestone Date 
 Unauthorized access detected Nov. 3, 2026 
 Breach disclosed; affected customers emailed Nov. 6, 2026 
 Branded card services end Dec. 20, 2026, 23:59 UTC 
 General cardholder support ends June 18, 2027 
 Refunds, disputes and chargebacks support ends June 12, 2028 
 Note: Dates are drawn from Gnosis Pay's disclosure and its September closure notice.
 The notice asks cardholders to export transaction histories before the closure and to update recurring payments with merchants. Data handling does not end with the card program: published guidance says identity and transaction records are kept for five years after account closure, and support correspondence for six years. After Dec. 20, customers seeking card records must request them directly from the company, since blockchain explorers do not display merchant names or card-level transaction details.
 The November disclosure is separate from a June exploit that drained about $1.5 million in digital assets from card accounts. In a July postmortem, Gnosis Pay traced that incident to a flaw in the Zodiac smart contract framework and said affected customers had been fully reimbursed. The company has not said the two events share a cause.
 What it means for cardholders and partners
 The breach lands on a consumer business that is already winding down, which limits its operational reach but not its reputational cost. Because the enterprise white-label platform was untouched, business customers running card programs on Gnosis Pay infrastructure face no confirmed exposure from this incident. For individual cardholders, the practical risk in the remaining weeks is phishing built on genuine account details, which is why the company is pushing customers toward its official apps and a dedicated support address, help@gnosispay.com , where staff are prioritizing those directly affected.
